ref: Mishneh Torah, Vessels of the Sanctuary and Those Who Serve Therein 6:6
en_version: Mishneh Torah, trans. by Eliyahu Touger. Jerusalem, Moznaim Pub. c1986-c2007
he: וּבַמֶּה הָיוּ קוֹרְאִין בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְּרֵאשִׁית. בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן קוֹרְאִין בְּרֵאשִׁית וִיהִי רָקִיעַ. בַּשֵּׁנִי יְהִי רָקִיעַ וְיִקָּווּ. בִּשְׁלִישִׁי יִקָּווּ וִיהִי מְאֹרֹת. בִּרְבִיעִי <small>(בראשית א יד)</small> "יְהִי מְאֹרֹת" <small>(בראשית א כ)</small> "וְיִשְׁרְצוּ". בַּחֲמִישִׁי יִשְׁרְצוּ <small>(בראשית א כד)</small> "וְתוֹצֵא הָאָרֶץ". בְּשִׁשִּׁי תּוֹצֵא הָאָרֶץ <small>(בראשית ב א)</small> "וַיְכֻלּוּ":
en: What would they read [from the Torah]? The narrative of creation.10In his Commentary to the Mishnah (loc. cit.:2), the Rambam explains that this subject was chosen, because the ultimate fulfillment of existence is the service of sacrificial worship, as implied by Ta'anit 27b: "Were it not for the sacrifices, the heavens and the earth would not be maintained." On the first day, they would read: "In the beginning," "Let there be a firmament;"11On each day, they would read the passage associated with that and the following day of creation. On the second day, "Let there be a firmament" and "Let [the waters] be gathered;" on the third day, "Let [the waters] be gathered" and "Let there be luminaries;" on the fourth day, "Let there be luminaries" and "Let the waters teem;" on the fifth day, "Let the waters teem" and "Let the earth produce;" on the sixth day, "Let the earth produce" and "[The heavens and the earth] were completed."
